description: Add real-time WebSocket graph diffs end-to-end, feature-flagged and gracefully degrading. Backend: a FastAPI WebSocket gateway that fans out graph diffs {addedNodes, removedNodes, updatedEdges} to connected clients; each client subscribes with its current filters (sector/time window/sentiment/entity focus) and the gateway forwards ONLY diffs intersecting that client's view (server-side viewport/filter predicate). Diffs are the transport unit - never full-graph reloads after initial load. A publisher abstraction sends diffs via Redis pub/sub (redis>=5.0 is already a backend dependency); the ingestion path (backend/app/tasks/ingest.py run_ingestion) publishes a diff after it persists new/changed nodes and edges. Client: a WS client that on connect does one initial /graph/query (existing /api/graph REST load), then streams diffs into the FEAT-002 Zustand store via applyDiff; reconnects with exponential backoff; on reconnect re-fetches initial state. Everything is gated on a WS URL env var (NEXT_PUBLIC_WS_URL client-side, WS_URL/redis settings backend-side): if unset or unreachable, the frontend still renders from /api/graph exactly as FEAT-003 leaves it. Design all WS + pub/sub code to be unit-testable without live Redis/WS (in-memory fake pub/sub + FastAPI TestClient websocket_connect).
steps: Backend pub/sub abstraction: create backend/app/realtime/diff_publisher.py defining a GraphDiff dataclass/pydantic model {added_nodes, removed_nodes, updated_edges} (serialized to the frontend camelCase {addedNodes, removedNodes, updatedEdges} shape, mirroring lib/types.ts EconomicNode/EconomicEdge) and a Publisher Protocol with publish(diff) / subscribe() . Provide a RedisDiffPublisher (redis.asyncio pub/sub on a channel from settings) and an InMemoryDiffPublisher fake for tests. Add settings to backend/app/config.py: a realtime_enabled flag and a diff channel name (redis_url already exists); default realtime OFF so nothing changes unless configured.

Backend WS gateway: create backend/app/routers/ws.py with a WebSocket endpoint (e.g. /ws/graph). On connect the client sends an initial subscribe message with its filters {sector/category, startDate, endDate, sentiment, entity}; the gateway registers a connection + its filter predicate, subscribes to the diff publisher, and for each incoming diff applies a SERVER-SIDE predicate that keeps only nodes/edges intersecting that client's view before forwarding. Support a filter-update message so the client can change its subscription without reconnecting. Handle disconnect cleanup. Reuse the filtering logic in backend/app/services/graph_service.py (the same category/date/sentiment/entity rules) so server-side predicate matches REST filtering exactly. Mount the router in backend/app/main.py create_app().

Wire diff publishing into ingestion: in backend/app/tasks/ingest.py (run_ingestion), after persistence, compute the diff of what changed (added article-nodes, updated edges; removed nodes if any) and publish it via the configured Publisher, guarded by the realtime_enabled flag so a disabled/misconfigured Redis is a no-op (best-effort, never fail ingestion). Keep the publish path importable without a live broker (construct the publisher lazily inside the task).

Backend tests (backend/tests/): add test_ws_gateway.py using FastAPI TestClient websocket_connect + an InMemoryDiffPublisher injected via app.dependency_overrides (mirror the get_read_store override pattern in backend/tests/test_graph_api.py and the fakes in conftest.py). Cover: (1) client connects, sends filters, receives a diff that intersects its view; (2) the server-side predicate DROPS a diff that does not intersect the client's filters (e.g. wrong category/sentiment/out-of-window); (3) a filter-update message changes what the client subsequently receives; (4) diff JSON serializes to the exact camelCase {addedNodes, removedNodes, updatedEdges} contract; (5) disconnect cleans up the connection registry. Add an in-memory pub/sub fake to conftest.py if useful. Keep everything free of live Redis/Neo4j/Qdrant/Postgres.

Frontend WS gating helper: create lib/realtime/ws-config.ts mirroring the BACKEND_URL gating pattern in lib/backend-client.ts - read NEXT_PUBLIC_WS_URL, expose isRealtimeEnabled() and a normalized URL. When unset, realtime is disabled and callers do nothing.

Frontend WS client: create lib/realtime/graphSocket.ts - opens a WebSocket to NEXT_PUBLIC_WS_URL, sends the current filters as the subscribe message, and on each diff message calls store.applyDiff(diff) (FEAT-002). Implement exponential backoff reconnect (capped) and, on (re)connect, trigger a re-fetch of the initial /api/graph state via the existing hook/store.initFromGraph so the client re-syncs. Send a filter-update message when the HUD filters change (subscribe the socket to store filter changes). No-op safely in SSR/when disabled. Never throw to the UI.

Wire the client into app/network/page.tsx: after the initial REST load + store.initFromGraph, if isRealtimeEnabled(), start graphSocket; on unmount, close it. If disabled or the socket errors, the page keeps rendering the REST-loaded graph unchanged (graceful fallback - real-time is additive only).

Frontend tests (`bun test`): add unit tests for lib/realtime/* - (1) isRealtimeEnabled() true only when NEXT_PUBLIC_WS_URL is set; (2) the diff message handler calls store.applyDiff and the store reflects added/removed nodes and updated edges (drive the FEAT-002 store directly with a fake socket / injected message); (3) reconnect backoff schedule increases and is capped (use fake timers / injected scheduler); (4) filter-update message payload matches the backend subscribe/update contract. Stub the WebSocket global so no real network is used.

Docs + env: add NEXT_PUBLIC_WS_URL (client) to .env.example with an explanatory comment (unset = REST-only, no realtime), and add the backend realtime settings (realtime enabled flag + diff channel; redis_url already documented) to backend/.env.example. Update README.md (frontend) and backend/README.md with a short 'Step 2: custom WebGL engine + real-time WS diffs' section describing the architecture (instanced engine, worker sim, Zustand-outside-React, WS gateway + Redis diffs, graceful fallback) and EXACTLY what needs the user's real browser+GPU (60 FPS / visual correctness) and managed Redis/backend (live WS end-to-end) to validate.
acceptance_criteria: A FastAPI WebSocket endpoint (backend/app/routers/ws.py, mounted in create_app) accepts a client subscribe message with filters, forwards ONLY diffs intersecting that client's view via a server-side predicate reusing the graph_service filter rules, supports filter-update without reconnect, and cleans up on disconnect - all covered by FastAPI TestClient websocket_connect tests with an in-memory publisher (no live Redis).

A Publisher abstraction with a RedisDiffPublisher (redis pub/sub) and an InMemoryDiffPublisher fake exists; diffs serialize to the exact camelCase {addedNodes, removedNodes, updatedEdges} contract mirroring lib/types.ts.
run_ingestion publishes a diff after persistence, guarded by a realtime flag so a disabled/unreachable Redis is a best-effort no-op that never fails ingestion.

The frontend WS client streams diffs into the FEAT-002 store via applyDiff, does an initial /api/graph load, reconnects with capped exponential backoff, re-syncs on reconnect, and sends filter-update messages when HUD filters change.
Realtime is fully gated on NEXT_PUBLIC_WS_URL: unset/unreachable leaves app/network rendering from /api/graph exactly as FEAT-003 leaves it (graceful fallback, real-time additive only).
`bun test` frontend realtime tests pass (gating, diff->store apply, backoff schedule, filter payload) with a stubbed WebSocket; backend `uv run pytest` WS tests pass.

.env.example gains NEXT_PUBLIC_WS_URL and backend/.env.example gains the realtime settings; README.md and backend/README.md document the Step 2 architecture and what needs a real browser/GPU + managed infra to validate.
`bun run build` + `bun run lint` clean; backend `uv run ruff check . && uv run mypy .` clean.
verification: Run `cd backend && uv run pytest -q` and confirm WS gateway + publisher tests pass.
Run `cd backend && uv run ruff check . && uv run mypy .` and confirm clean.
Run `bun test` and confirm frontend realtime unit tests pass.
Run `bun run build` and `bun run lint` and confirm both clean.
Manually confirm (by reading app/network/page.tsx) that with NEXT_PUBLIC_WS_URL unset the page path does not construct a WebSocket and renders from /api/graph.
